roles.produced: docs/IDENTITY_LIVE_SHAPE_CHECK.md — driven against a live Keycloak 26.4. Three fields sso-session names are NOT wire facts: amr is absent from the access token, the ID token, /userinfo and RFC 7662 introspection alike, leaving only an opaque deployment-configured acr, so single_factor/mfa/phishing_resistant is not derivable from a default IdP; auth_time is absent everywhere, so iat (token issuance) is not when the human authenticated — the same defect class as the RADIUS lastAuthAt finding; and the access token exp is 60s against a 36000s session max, demonstrated live at 75s with the token dead and four SSO sessions still alive. The session record carries no device field at all (id, username, userId, ipAddress, start, lastAccess, rememberMe, clients, transientUser), and two logins by the same user from the same host produced two indistinguishable sessions — precisely the leftover-session case the dimension exists for, so the device-session join must come from the device side. The code is already right (the connector normalizes a bridge-supplied value through oneOf with an unknown fallback and evaluate.ts raises the bar on every unknown); what was missing was the wire-truth record. proof:live-keycloak 14/14.
roles.nextAction: Ten of fifteen dimensions remain unverified against any live IdP, and only Keycloak was driven — Entra DOES emit amr and Okta exposes richer session APIs, so the wire-truth table is one IdP wide. roles.charter: Who actually buys this, what they already run, and which of their failures SignalGrid removes. Evidence about real buyers, never invented personas.
roles.trigger: A positioning, pricing or roadmap decision is about to be made on an assumption about buyers that nobody has checked.
roles.produced: docs/company/ICP_EVIDENCE.md — the first buyer evidence in this repository that is sourced rather than inferred, every finding carrying a SOURCE TIER because most of what a search returns on this topic is written by someone selling the fix. TIER 1: three granted US patents (11329990, 11838295, 12425415) disclose shared-device audit misattribution as prior art — the strongest evidence available and a warning that the space is claimed. TIER 2: one healthcare posting spanning Intune, M365 and Imprivata and asking for baselines standardised ACROSS Intune and Jamf Pro, which establishes the SHAPE and explicitly not the frequency. TIER 3: industry writing placing the failure at the shift boundary. It also names what it does NOT establish — the 75-1,000 employee segment in EXECUTIVE_ONE_PAGER.md is corroborated by nothing gathered, and every source is healthcare, so the claim that the pattern generalises to retail and field service is unevidenced. One claim in it was FALSE and is corrected inline rather than edited away: it said no competitive surface named OLOID or Imprivata, while four anchored briefs and a battlecard had sat in docs/research/ since 2026-07-14. See backlog row 57.
roles.nextAction: Two things, in order. FIRST, turn Finding 2 from a shape into a frequency: sample 15-20 job postings rather than one, and record the count that name two MDMs, the count that name an identity product beside them, and the count that name neither — a proportion, not an anecdote. SECOND, find a published case study or conference talk where an estate describes the handoff failing in their own words; Finding 3 currently rests on tier 3 and that is the weakest tier in the file. NOT part of this role: the competitive refresh, which belongs to competitive-analyst and is scoped in row 57.
